title: Non-blocking finding from PR #285's review (PositionsTable.handleConfirmClose's unconditional pendingDelete clear)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #285 (frontend-close-position-dialog-followups). PR #285's own `decisions` entry explicitly flagged this quirk as a real, pre-existing latent bug discovered while writing the PR's new regression test, but deliberately left it unfixed and unfiled ('if a future reviewer wants it tracked, the natural home is a new <id>-followups entry'). This reviewer's independent assessment agrees it's genuinely reachable (not just theoretical) and confirms via `git diff` that `handleConfirmClose`'s logic predates PR #285 (untouched by it) -- tracked here rather than blocking PR #285's otherwise-clean cleanup work, since fixing it is out of scope for that PR's 3 checklist items.

checklist.step: `PositionsTable.handleConfirmClose`'s `onSuccess: () => setPendingDelete(null)` callback is bound per-call to whichever position's `mutate()` invocation it was passed to, not to whatever `pendingDelete` currently holds when it later fires. Reachable sequence: (1) open Position A's ClosePositionDialog and confirm -- `deletePosition.mutate()` starts, held pending by a slow/delayed DELETE response; (2) dismiss A's dialog via a backdrop click while the DELETE is still in flight (`handleCancelClose` allows this, and doesn't call `reset()` while `isPending`); (3) open Position B's (a different position) ClosePositionDialog -- its Confirm button renders disabled/loading too, since `isPending` is shared/unscoped across the whole table (this is the exact invariant PR #285's own new regression test and doc comment describe); (4) A's DELETE resolves successfully -- its `onSuccess` fires, calling `setPendingDelete(null)` unconditionally, which closes B's dialog out from under the user at the same moment B's Confirm button would have become clickable, silently discarding any exit-reason/manual-override values the user had already entered for B, with no error or explanation shown. Not a data-corruption risk (B's position is never actually deleted), but a real, user-visible 'dialog vanishes unexpectedly mid-interaction' bug. Fix by scoping the `onSuccess` clear to only fire when `pendingDelete` still refers to the position that mutation call was for (e.g. capture the intended position id in the closure and compare against current `pendingDelete?.id`, or use a functional `setPendingDelete` updater that no-ops when the ids don't match), and add a regression test exercising this exact sequence (two positions, held DELETE responses, backdrop-dismiss then reopen-for-a-different-position, assert the second dialog stays open after the first's DELETE resolves).
